Selected Projects

Suspension Design · Kinematics · Load Analysis
Rear Trailing-Arm Geometry — Blue Sky Solar Racing Gen 13

Built a MATLAB kinematics and load model of the Gen 13 rear trailing-arm suspension and optimized the pivot and mount geometry to reduce the forces fed into the chassis clevises, sweeping the linkage through ±51 mm of wheel travel, while holding the motion ratio to the Aurora baseline so the car rides the same. The selected geometry is predicted to cut clevis loads by about 22% at both primary mounts and 14% at the third. The lateral (cornering) load case is not modelled yet and is the next check before the geometry is frozen.

Vehicle Dynamics · Multibody Simulation
Aurora Vehicle Dynamics Model — Blue Sky Solar Racing

Building a full multibody model of Aurora, the team's three-wheeled solar car, from scratch in Altair MotionView/MotionSolve: double-wishbone front corners, a single-wheel trailing-arm rear, rack-and-pinion steering, tires and a path-following driver. Bump-camber kinematics match the hand-calculated geometry. Placeholder spring and tire data are being replaced with the team's measured values; next come closed-loop slalom, figure-8 and U-turn runs, correlated against Aurora's recorded times, so the model can judge Gen 13 suspension geometry before anything is built.

Automotive · Structural FEA · Composite Design
Blue Sky Solar Racing — Aerobody Structural Optimization

Developed a Python-based automated optimization pipeline integrating ANSYS ACP and ANSYS Mechanical to iteratively modify composite core layup structures across 100+ simulation runs. Implemented Bayesian optimization to guide design exploration, cutting bottom-aerobody mass by ~50% while staying within deformation limits. Reworked the mold stack-up in CATIA and SolidWorks to use up to 60% less prepreg, then laid up parts in the team shop. The car raced at FSGP and ASC 2026.

Product Design · CAD · Off-Grid Energy
AquaSweep — Solar-Powered Pond Cleaning for Shrimp Farms

Co-founder and CTO of Aqua Nusa, a three-person startup building AquaSweep: two rotating arms push sludge across the floor of lined shrimp ponds toward the central drain using low-velocity water jets, so workers no longer wade in to siphon by hand. One solar-and-battery hub on the bank serves up to four ponds. Led the technical design — a 19-part SOLIDWORKS rotating-arm assembly, fabrication drawings for the key hub parts, jet and wall-shear sizing, and the solar/battery energy balance — and caught 3 manufacturability issues in design review. The problem was defined through interviews with 5 shrimp farmers and aquaculture operators in Indonesia. Entered in Pertamuda Energy Founder 2026; prototype planned for winter 2026–27 in Toronto.

Structural FEA · CCUS · Competition Research
Carbon-Seal — Self-Healing Cement for CO₂ Wellbore Storage

A waste-derived self-healing cement (eggshell powder + rice husk ash) for sealing CO₂ leakage in CCUS wellbores, combining experimental characterization with finite element analysis. Pre-cracked specimens were healed under water immersion and tracked by optical microscopy, achieving 75–80% microcrack closure — roughly double conventional cement. A coupled thermo-structural ANSYS model of the wellbore cement sheath (steel casing, cement annulus, formation rock) under downhole loads (35–120°C gradient, 20 MPa injection, 30 MPa confining) gave the lowest von Mises stress and a 27% higher safety factor than the OPC control. Finalist at PETROLIDA 2026.
